abstract: arXiv:2610.22373v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly used as autonomous orchestrators in distributed and multi-agent systems, yet a control gap remains: no protocol-level mechanism allows human operators to inject binding directives that persist across planning cycles. abstract: arXiv:2610.22379v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Calibrating expensive engineering simulators requires tuning model parameters to match reference data, a process heavily constrained by computational costs. abstract: arXiv:2610.22380v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Continuous diffusion treats the forward process as a design space; discrete language diffusion often uses absorbing corruption, leaving context fully trusted throughout generation. This makes trust binary: corrupted context is copied as ground truth, propagating errors into generated spans. title: Binding-Specific Relearning Savings for Test-Time Continual Learning
abstract: arXiv:2610.22381v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: When a fact becomes harder to elicit from a language model, has the model lost it, or has it merely become less accessible? Parameter-updating test-time continual learning agents are usually evaluated by current output accuracy; we ask whether that measurement captures how prior experience shapes later updates. title: Rethinking User Encoders: Routing Diffusion States for Scenario-Adaptive User Representation
abstract: arXiv:2610.22400v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Existing large language model (LLM)-based user encoders serialize heterogeneous behavioral logs and compress them into static representations through autoregressive (AR) prediction. title: From Events to Reasoning: Hierarchical Rule Composition over Explicit States
abstract: arXiv:2610.22403v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: What a reasoning system emits is a conclusion; what it owes is a justification. Producing one requires every operation to be admissible on the facts actually available, the dependencies of intermediate results to survive to the end of the path, and the path to be revised when a premise changes. abstract: arXiv:2610.22408v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Long-horizon GUI agents rely on visual history to maintain task states, but retaining historical screenshots increases visual-token usage and inference costs, while textual summaries can discard critical state information, undermining long-horizon reliability. title: Sensitivity Analysis of Decision Rules in an Agent-Based Agro-Ecological Model
abstract: arXiv:2610.22420v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Agent-based models are well-suited for modelling agro-ecological systems for decision-making, yet turning their simulations into actionable insight requires identifying which decisions actually drive the behaviours. title: PRIME: Towards Verifiable Evidence-Grounded Reasoning in LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.22426v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM agents are used to check records against an organization's requirements, for example whether a vulnerability report is ready for investigation. Requirements often allow several ways to be met, such as a severity rating with a curator-reviewed advisory or a published advisory link. abstract: arXiv:2610.22430v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Accurate prediction of multivariate time series requires models that simultaneously capture variable-specific dynamics and cross-variable interactions. In this work, a Correlation-Guided and Dynamics-Trained Clustered Echo State Network (CGDT-CESN) is proposed, which comprises a modular reservoir architecture with each cluster distinctly specializing in one of the variables in the multivariate time series. abstract: arXiv:2610.22433v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Flexible job-shop scheduling becomes resource-coupled when a scarce vehicle fleet moves jobs between stations, because the schedule sets the transport waits. BOLT (bound-oriented learning for transport-coupled scheduling) builds a lower bound from chain, machine-capacity, and fleet-capacity relaxations. title: TRACE: Transformer Residual Activation Codebook Encoding for Communication-efficient Distributed Edge Inference
abstract: arXiv:2610.22435v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Distributed Transformer inference across co-located edge devices is fundamentally communication-bound, as exchanging activations between sequence-parallel partitions dominates inference latency under commodity edge bandwidths. title: Generative adversarial networks with Monte Carlo dropout uncertainty quantification for structural health monitoring: Fibre Bragg grating data augmentation comparison in Hawk T1A aircraft
abstract: arXiv:2610.22436v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The signal generation capabilities of a novel data augmentation framework are examined in aerospace structures. First, the framework learns class-conditional temporal and spectral characteristics of the measured structural responses. It uses conditional generative adversarial network training and Monte Carlo dropout uncertainty quantification as a Bayesian approximation. This step enables stochastic signal synthesis and uncertainty quantification.

abstract: arXiv:2610.22437v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Automated fundus-based diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading can substantially expand screening capacity, but source-trained models degrade sharply across different cameras, clinics, and patient populations. abstract: arXiv:2610.22438v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Studies of what fine-tuning does to a language model often summarise the weight update $\Delta W$ by its rank. title: Sparse Autoencoders Can Induce Local Geometry for Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting
abstract: arXiv:2610.22439v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Catastrophic forgetting remains a challenge in supervised continual learning, as adapting to new tasks causes representation drift and loss of previously learned information. This raises the question of which representational changes should be constrained while preserving plasticity. abstract: arXiv:2610.22441v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) provide a convenient interface for translating natural language commands into task plans for cyber-physical systems (CPSs). abstract: arXiv:2610.22444v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding (STVG) aims to jointly localize a target in space and time given a natural-language query. Despite continued advances, existing STVG benchmarks remain largely centered on localizing targets through instance-specific descriptions, leaving them largely decoupled from long-form reasoning increasingly emphasized in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). abstract: arXiv:2610.22445v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Automated discovery systems propose scientific explanations and test which to accept. Does passing a test establish the intended claim? abstract: arXiv:2610.22446v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Neural operators approximate solution operators of partial differential equations at a fraction of the cost of numerical solvers. abstract: arXiv:2610.22448v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Enhancing the agentic capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) to tackle complex software engineering (SWE) and general terminal-usage problems is a pressing challenge. title: Where Prefill Expert Reduction Hurts MoE Models: A Few Prompt Tokens Carry Most of the Short-Answer F1 Loss
abstract: arXiv:2610.22454v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Running prompt tokens through fewer routed experts during prefill is a simple way to make mixture-of-experts (MoE) serving cheaper, yet it is unclear what this damages. title: Functional Welfare for AI Safety
abstract: arXiv:2610.22460v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI welfare is generally treated purely as an ethical issue rather than also as a safety issue. We argue this is a mistake. Whatever their moral status, models exhibit welfare-like states that causally influence their behaviour. Following recent work, we adopt the term 'functional welfare' for these states. title: Author-in-the-loop Agentic Reproducibility Auditing for a Machine Learning Conference
abstract: arXiv:2610.22465v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reproducibility checks during peer review require a shared understanding of what authors' code is expected to reproduce. We present an author-in-the-loop collaborative audit that makes author declarations explicit inputs to an AI agent's investigation and assessment. title: Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution
abstract: arXiv:2610.22466v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Harness evolution automatically optimizes the prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration code around a fixed-weight model, offering a way to improve agentic systems without updating model weights. title: Progressive Misalignment Can Emerge from Benign Recursive Self-Distillation
abstract: arXiv:2610.22467v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Training models on their own outputs has attracted widespread attention as a possible route to advance AI capabilities. One prominent approach is self-distillation, where a model is trained to match the token-level predictions it would have produced when given access to additional context, such as a cue, feedback, or instruction. abstract: arXiv:2610.22468v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Action nominal constructions (ANCs) express events in nominal form, with their argument marking following patterns found in clauses or ordinary noun phrases. title: Testing the Planning Claims of LLM-Based Agents against Formal Semantics
abstract: arXiv:2610.22469v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly credited with the competences of practical reasoning: planning, monitoring, and correcting their own actions. title: Generative Value Classifier

title: JAVIS: Joint Audio-Visual Interaction and Streaming for Real-Time Conversational Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.22499v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Human communication is inherently multimodal, conveying intent not only through linguistic and vocal cues but also through visual signals. However, existing conversational systems have mainly focused on text or speech, leaving out the visual feedback that is essential for natural interaction. title: RealCLI: Toward a Unified Evaluation of Human-Agent Collaboration for CLI Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.22507v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Command-line interface (CLI) agents increasingly execute longer-horizon tasks, yet existing benchmarks either assume that user instructions remain fixed throughout execution or evaluate task outcomes without capturing runtime collaboration quality. In this paper, we present REALCLI, a paired benchmark that unifies the evaluation of task execution and human-agent collaboration quality on realistic CLI tasks. title: TriSAR-3D and PaintFusion: A Novel Trimodal LiDAR-RGB-Thermal Dataset and Method for 3D Person Detection in Search and Rescue
abstract: arXiv:2610.22509v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reliable 3D person detection is important for rescue robotics to give first responders situational awareness. Yet most multimodal 3D detection research targets automotive scenarios in which pedestrians mostly appear in a narrow range of upright, near-road poses. It is therefore unclear how much of the reported performance transfers to rescue settings, as a person may be lying, partially occluded, or in unstructured indoor and outdoor environments.

abstract: arXiv:2610.22511v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Evaluating language models and agents requires combining benchmark accuracy, judge-based assessment, runtime performance, tool-use behavior, and retrieval quality. title: Predicting Privileged Information Effectiveness for On-Policy Self-Distillation
abstract: arXiv:2610.22512v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) enables large language models (LLMs) to learn from privileged information (PI) without a separate teacher model. However, prior work largely treats PI as a fixed design choice, leaving the effects of its content and construction poorly understood. title: Towards Reconstructing Geographically Diverse Architecture with 3D Foundation Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.22514v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Internet-scale photo collections of real-world landmarks have driven progress in 3D computer vision yet remain highly challenging for modern 3D foundation models (3DFMs) that estimate scene structure in a single feed-forward pass. abstract: arXiv:2610.22515v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We describe our submission to Subtask~1b of ImageEval 2026. The task consists of selecting the single visually valid statement from three candidates paired with an image, and is in both English and Modern Standard Arabic (MSA). title: Learning User Representations to Improve Simulation Fidelity
abstract: arXiv:2610.22518v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: User simulators enable interactive training and evaluation of AI assistants at scale. Yet current simulators struggle to reproduce the diverse behaviors of real users, leading to assistants that generalize poorly to underrepresented users. We identify user representations as an underexplored bottleneck in user simulation. abstract: arXiv:2610.22519v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Inferring dynamics from real-world experimental data is inherently ambiguous, as many plausible dynamical systems can explain the same positional observations at measurement times. abstract: arXiv:2610.22523v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Understanding biomolecular function requires characterizing three-dimensional structure and conformational variability, for which cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) is a powerful tool. title: FlashControl: One-Step Controllable Generator via Distillation-Friendly Single-Stream Teachers
abstract: arXiv:2610.22537v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Diffusion models have become a leading approach in visual generative modeling, particularly effective in text-to-image and controllable generation. abstract: arXiv:2610.22538v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) that leverage test-time computation achieve strong performance on mathematical and scientific benchmarks and are increasingly deployed in real-world applications. abstract: arXiv:2610.22539v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The web is not static or uniform. Websites that serve the same purpose can look and navigate very differently.
